title: Sergeant John Glasgow, Royal Scots discharge, Belfast, 10 March 1817

citations.name: John Glasgow
citations.type: Sergeant John Glasgow, Royal Scots discharge, Belfast, 10 March 1817
citations.assertion: Compatible existing identity of the single recorded John; no second soldier or parent relationship asserted.. The original discharge describes Sergeant John Glasgow of the 1st Battalion Royal Scots, born in the parish and town of Glasgow, Lanark, about thirty-five years old and formerly a labourer. He enlisted at eighteen; the service table begins 7 May 1800. The discharge was signed at Belfast on 10 March 1817, for hernia, and recommends Glasgow for his pension. The following sheet contains his signed receipt and the certification that the disability did not arise from misconduct. The originals name no father, mother, wife or children and give no Struthers Street address. Identification with the Calton household and the memorial profile remains inferred, not a completed merger. The 1848 memorial is a derivative lead without an inspected grave photograph. The 1782 indexed child attached to 2875 remains a separate unproved childhood-to-adult identification: its inspected FamilySearch entry gives only August 1782, Glasgow and no parents. No father is invented or assigned; both live profiles currently have no parents. No relationship percentage, structural attachment, birth field or death field changes, and no confidence-progress gain is counted. John Glasgow: Compatible existing identity of the single recorded John; no second soldier or parent relationship asserted.; John Glasgow: Compatible existing identity of the single recorded John; no second soldier or parent relationship asserted. Reviewed 2026-10-31; Original scans privately retained; new original reading, existing 7 October index lead.
